name: Mapudungun
notes: Research. Mapudungun (Mapuche/Araucanian), an isolate of central-southern Chile and Argentine Patagonia. This spec models the Alfabeto Mapuche Unificado (Unified Alphabet, Grafemario Unificado, Salas 2006) rather than the Azümchefe alternative: the WOLD gold sample's letters (⟨tr⟩, ⟨ll⟩, ⟨ng⟩, ⟨ch⟩, ⟨ü⟩, ⟨ḻ⟩/⟨ṉ⟩ for the dental laterals/nasal, ⟨ñ⟩) match the Unified Alphabet's conventions, not Azümchefe's (which instead uses ⟨tx⟩, ⟨lh⟩, ⟨g⟩, ⟨ch⟩/⟨c⟩, ⟨v⟩, etc.). Key correspondences: ⟨tr⟩ is the retroflex affricate [ʈʂ] (not t+r), ⟨ll⟩ is the palatal lateral [ʎ], ⟨ng⟩ is the velar nasal [ŋ], ⟨ch⟩ is [tʃ], ⟨ü⟩ is the high central vowel [ɨ], plain ⟨r⟩ is a retroflex approximant [ɻ] (not a tap/trill), and ⟨ḻ⟩/⟨ṉ⟩ (l/n with a combining macron below) write the dental lateral/nasal contrasting with the alveolar ⟨l⟩/⟨n⟩. This entry was previously a structural-adstrate placeholder (for Chilean/Argentine Spanish contact-linguistics nodes) claiming no phonology; the WOLD `Mapudungun` gold confirmed the Unified Alphabet matches real orthographic practice, so the placeholder has been replaced with a cited grapheme map. Mapudungun word stress is non-contrastive and largely predictable from the penultimate mora in descriptive accounts, but is not treated as reliably orthography-predictable across all dialects surveyed by Smeets (2008), so no `stress` block is asserted here (documented exemption).
